newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed, eye on tender.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed, eye on tender.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Tuesday, with traders looking ahead nervously to the weekly T-bill tender amid expectations of a U.S. short-term interest rate hike, analysts said.

"The tender today is fairly large. I think it's going to be a tiptoe through the tulips kind of tender. There's not going to be big aggressive bidding going on," said a T-bill dealer with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield of 3.19 percent, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.

The Bank of Canada this afternoon will auction C$6.2 billion of three-month, six-month and one year T-bills even as C$5.4 billion in T-bills come due. Results of the weekly auction will be announced at 1330 EST/1830 GMT.

Dealers said this week's auction will be complicated by the fact that the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee is only expected to announce a rate decision sometime around 1415 EST/1915 GMT.
A large number of traders are parking money in the overnight market ahead of an expected hike in U.S. rates, the dealer said.
The Bank of Canada is not expected to match a U.S. rate hike of 25 basis points.

In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.49 percent. The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.94 percent from 3.96 percent at the close of trading on Monday.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range, dealers said.
